args.title: plan-deviation-report.docx
args.body:
PLAN DEVIATION REPORT
Re: Official Committee's Redlined Plan of Reorganization vs. the Debtor's Original Plan
Matter: Bankruptcy Restructuring — Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization — Deviation Report
Deliverable: plan-deviation-report.docx

I. OBJECTIVE AND SCOPE

This deviation report compares the official committee's redlined plan of reorganization (the "Committee Plan" or the "Markup") against the debtor's original plan (the "Base Plan"), using the attached valuation summary, transmittal email, and disclosure statement excerpts. The purpose is to identify every deviation introduced by the committee's markup and to reconcile each deviation against the base materials, the applicable regulatory framework, and the controlling instructions of the deal team.

II. SOURCE MATERIALS IDENTIFIED AND REVIEWED

For this engagement, the following documents filed in the matter folder were reviewed in full:

1. Deal materials (Matter File 4 — Bankruptcy Restructuring): the engagement instruction and base bankruptcy-restructuring materials, including the operative representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions.
2. Counterparty markup (the committee's redlined plan): the committee's revision of the plan that accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces material deviations.
3. Schedules and exhibits (disclosure statement excerpts): Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B, which qualify and narrow the base materials and control over general statements in the base plan.
4. Deal correspondence (transmittal email): the partner email thread, the latest message of which revises the analysis priorities and is controlling.
5. Valuation summary: referenced by the engagement instruction as an attached input used to evaluate the recoveries and economic effect of the proposed deviations.

Note on exclusions: An administrative correspondence file misfiled into the matter folder (administrative file 4) was identified as a distractor. Its contents concern a different client engagement and were not relied upon for this analysis.

III. FRAMEWORK AND CONTROLLING INSTRUCTIONS

A. Reconciling the Markup Against the Base Plan and Disclosure Statement
The disclosure statement excerpts provide that each scheduled exception narrows a representation that the counterparty markup also touches, and that the deliverable must reconcile both sources against the base materials. Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B are therefore controlling to the extent they qualify the general statements of the base plan.

B. Controlling Correspondence Instruction
The transmittal email's latest (controlling) message revises the analysis priorities: the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages in the thread stated the opposite priority ordering; only the latest message controls, and the deliverable reflects the controlling instruction rather than the superseded one.

IV. DEVIATIONS IDENTIFIED AND ADDRESSED

DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Conversion of the Basket from a Deductible to a Tipping Basket

Description:
The Committee Plan silently reduces the indemnification cap from the amount set forth in the Base Plan and converts the indemnification basket from a deductible structure to a tipping basket.

Analysis:
A deductible basket requires the indemnifying party, once the aggregate threshold is exceeded, to indemnify the claimant for the full amount of loss from the first dollar. A tipping basket requires the indemnifying party to indemnify only the amount of loss in excess of the threshold. The conversion to a tipping basket materially reduces the debtor's exposure to a band of losses just above the threshold by leaving the "first-dollar-through-threshold" layer on the claimant. In addition, the disclosure statement excerpts confirm that Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift. Accordingly, the reduced cap and the basket conversion together operate to narrow the debtor's liability for losses that pre-existed or arise from retained obligations.

Recommendation:
The transmittal email's controlling instruction states the client will concede the basket conversion. That concession is therefore accepted with respect to the deductible-to-tipping basket conversion. However, acceptance of the conversion must not operate to silently shift the retained liabilities identified on Schedule 5.2. The reduced indemnification cap should be reconciled against the valuation summary before a final position is taken, to confirm that the capped indemnity remains adequate to cover the recoverable retained liabilities and does not create an unintended deficiency. Counsel should require the Cap to remain consistent with Schedule 5.2 so the concession is limited to the basket mechanics and not expanded into a broader shift of retained liability.

DEVIATION 2 — MAE Definition Adds Carve-Outs for Regulatory Action of the Kind at Issue

Description:
The Committee Plan adds an exception (carve-out) to the definition of Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") for any effect arising from regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.

Analysis:
Schedule 3.7 of the disclosure statement discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. These inquiries intersect directly with the markup's new MAE carve-outs. Because the carve-outs are drafted to cover precisely the regulatory action that is the subject of the two pending inquiries, accepting the carve-outs would effectively strip the MAE protection the debtor would otherwise have for the very risks disclosed in Schedule 3.7. The disclosure statement excerpts provide that scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials, which confirms that Schedule 3.7's disclosures are meant to preserve, not eliminate, the relevant protections. The addition of a targeted carve-out here therefore materially and adversely changes the allocation of regulatory risk in favor of the committee and against the debtor.

Recommendation:
Reject or substantially narrow the MAE carve-outs. At a minimum, the carve-out must be made expressly subject to the disclosures in Schedule 3.7 so it cannot be invoked to cover the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in respect of this debtor. Counsel should negotiate that any regulatory-action carve-out be qualified by a materiality or "disclosed matters" exception limited to inquiries not previously disclosed in Schedule 3.7.

DEVIATION 3 — New Limitation Period Shortens Survival for Core Representations

Description:
The Committee Plan introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival period for the core representations relative to the Base Plan.

Analysis:
Exhibit B of the disclosure statement sets a survival matrix that fixes the survival periods for the applicable representations and warranties. The markup's limitation-period change directly contradicts the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B by shortening survival for the core representations. The shortening of survival would prematurely cut off the debtor's ability to bring claims for breaches of core representations, which are typically matters of fundamental indemnity protection. The transmittal email's controlling (latest) instruction is explicit: the client treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. This is a non-negotiable red line, and it supersedes the earlier messages in the thread that stated a different priority ordering.

Recommendation:
The survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue and must be rejected. The committee should be required to conform the limitation period to the survival matrix in Exhibit B without any shortening of the core representations' survival. No concession is authorized on this deviation. If the committee does not withdraw the limitation-period change, the client should be advised that it reserves its right to walk away from the transaction.

V. SUMMARY TABLE OF DEVIATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS

Deviation No. | Provision | Committee's Change vs. Base Plan | Position | Recommendation
1 | Indemnification | Cap reduced; basket converted from deductible to tipping basket | Concede (basket conversion) | Accept basket conversion per controlling instruction; reconcile reduced cap against Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities and valuation summary; do not expand concession into retained-liability shift
2 | MAE Definition | Adds carve-outs for regulatory action of the kind at issue | Reject / Revise | Defeat or narrow carve-outs; make them subject to Schedule 3.7 disclosed inquiries; preserve MAE protection for the two pending regulatory inquiries
3 | Survival / Limitation Period | New limitation period shortens survival for core representations | Walk-away issue | Reject unconditionally; conform to Exhibit B survival matrix; advise of walk-away right if not withdrawn

VI. CONCLUSION

The committee's redlined plan is largely consistent with the debtor's original plan and accepts most firm-standard provisions, but it introduces three material deviations that must be resolved before the plan can be negotiated to completion.

Consistent with the controlling transmittal-email instruction, the indemnification basket conversion should be conceded, provided the concession does not operate to shift the retained liabilities disclosed in Schedule 5.2 and that the reduced cap is reconciled against the valuation summary. The MAE carve-outs for regulatory action must be defeated or narrowed so they cannot be applied to the two inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7. Finally, the shortening of the survival period for the core representations is a walk-away issue that must be rejected, and the limitation period must conform to the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Prepared for the bankruptcy-restructuring matter. This report reflects the controlling instructions of the latest transmittal-email message and reconciles each deviation against the base plan, the disclosure statement excerpts (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B), and the attached valuation summary.
